page.text:
A basis translates an abstract vector space into a concrete coordinate
space, yet the number of vectors in any basis is an intrinsic invariant
of the space itself: its *dimension*. Dimension characterizes vector
spaces up to isomorphism, quantifying their topological and algebraic
degrees of freedom.

Complementary to the vectors themselves is the *dual space*, which
collects all linear measurements (functionals) on the space. Duality
reverses arrows: a linear map $T : V \to W$ induces a transpose map
$T^* : W^* \to V^*$ acting on measurements. Through annihilators, dual
bases, and the bidual isomorphism, duality reveals the geometric symmetry
underpinning linear systems and orthogonality.
